name: Skeleton
summary: Grey shimmering shapes that stand in for content while it loads, so the layout does not jump.
useWhen: First load of a page or card whose layout is known (article list, profile header, dashboard card).
Loading takes long enough to notice (about 300ms or more).

dontUseWhen.case: An action the user just triggered (save, upload, publish)
dontUseWhen.use: button loading state or a spinner

dontUseWhen.case: The layout of the result is unknown or loading is very short

anatomy.description: Stacks skeletons in a column (or a row with --row) with the standard gap. Hide it from screen readers.
One placeholder shape. Full width, rectangle by default. Use a shape modifier to say what it stands for.

attributes.aria-hidden: true (unless its group already has it)

modifiers.description: A line of text: pill radius, body-sm height.
Rectangle for an image or hero. Same as the bare class; write it for clarity.
Circle, avatar-md size unless you set width and height.
Full-width bar at data-table row height.
Text line height for small text. Sets only the height: add --text for the pill shape.
75% width. Use on the last line of a paragraph.
Lays skeletons out in a row, vertically centred (e.g. avatar next to text lines).

states.name: loading
states.how: Skeletons are shown; the region they sit in has aria-busy="true".

states.name: loaded
states.how: Replace the skeletons with the real content and set aria-busy="false" (or remove it).

states.name: reduced motion
states.how: prefers-reduced-motion stops the shimmer and shows a static, dimmed shape. Automatic.

a11y: Skeletons are decorative: aria-hidden="true" on the group or on each skeleton.
Set aria-busy="true" on the region that is loading, and give it a short text for screen readers (e.g. Loading articles).
When loading ends, remove aria-busy so the new content is read.

rules.rule: Every .gds-skeleton has aria-hidden="true" itself or on an ancestor.
rules.why: Otherwise screen readers find empty, meaningless elements.

rules.rule: Skeletons sit inside an element with aria-busy="true" that also contains loading text for screen readers.
rules.why: Screen reader users must know the page is loading, not empty.

rules.rule: The skeleton copies the shape of the content it replaces: same number of lines, avatar size, image ratio.
rules.why: The page should not jump when content arrives.

rules.rule: Do not use .gds-skeleton inside .gds-table; use gds-table--loading and gds-table__skeleton.
rules.why: The table has its own loading pattern sized to its cells.
rules.removeInV3: Merge gds-table__skeleton into gds-skeleton so there is one loading shape.

rules.why: The size classes set only the height; without --text the line has square corners.
rules.removeInV3: Give the --text-* sizes the pill radius, so --text is not needed with them.

knownIssues.issue: --text-sm/lg/xl/2xl set only the height. Alone they give a square-cornered bar; the docs use --text-xl without --text.
knownIssues.fix: Move the pill radius into each --text-* class (or document the pair) and fix the docs examples.

knownIssues.issue: --row says it matches .gds-data-table rows, a class that no longer exists; the table also has its own gds-table__skeleton.
knownIssues.fix: Point --row at the gds-table row height, or remove it in favour of gds-table__skeleton.

knownIssues.issue: --rect is identical to the bare class, and --circle overlaps the --avatar-* presets.
knownIssues.fix: v3: keep one way: e.g. --circle + avatar size tokens, and drop --rect or make it the documented default.

knownIssues.issue: No helper for the screen-reader loading text; every product must remember aria-busy and an sr-only label.
knownIssues.fix: Document the pattern in the docs page and show it in every example.
